provenance.subject: A vault as release 0.7.0 persisted it: the previous release of this application, and the last one before the changes the current tree carries.
howGenerated: every ciphertext below was produced by that worktree's own packages/client/src/services/crypto/cryptoService.ts (PBKDF2-SHA256 600k over the master password with the lowercased email as salt, AES-256-GCM with a 12-byte IV and a 16-byte tag held separately, HMAC-SHA256 search hash over the trimmed lowercased name)
every `plaintext` was parsed by that worktree's own packages/shared/src/schemas/vault.ts before being sealed; the generator throws rather than emit a payload v0.7.0 would reject
`parsedByV070` is the output of that parse — recorded, not asserted, so the current schemas can be compared against what the previous release actually made of the same bytes
`account.settings` was instantiated from that worktree's own packages/server/src/models/User.ts, so the subtree carries that release's defaults rather than a hand-typed approximation of them
verifiedThat: each item decrypts, under the key derived from `account.masterPassword` and `account.email`, to exactly its `plaintext`
the wrapped vault key unwraps under the master encryption key derived from the same two inputs
notVerified: that any of these rows was written by a real user through the 0.7.0 UI — the shapes are derived from the schema history (backupCodes 0.6.0, street2 and deliveryNotes 0.7.0, absoluteExpiresAt 0.5.0), not captured from a production database
anything about releases older than 0.5.0 beyond what that schema history states
browser behaviour: the ciphertext was produced by Node’s Web Crypto implementation of the same algorithms, not by a browser
provenance.neverRegenerate: There is no --update path and there must not be one. Regenerating this file from the CURRENT tree would replace the previous release’s output with today’s and turn the test into a tautology; if the fixture ever has to change, generate it again from the v0.7.0 tag and say so here.

account.settingsNote: The settings subtree 0.7.0 wrote for a new account. It has no lockOnHidden and no lockOnHiddenDelay: the current release added both, with defaults, and nothing backfills them into an existing document.

items.note: A login as every release before 0.6.0 wrote one: loginDataSchema gained backupCodes in 0.6.0, so a vault at 0.7.0 still holds logins with no such key. backupCodes is .optional() with NO default, deliberately, so an absent one must stay absent.

parsedByV070.notes: Recovery contact is the work address.

items.note: The 0.7.0-era counterpart of the row above, carrying the backupCodes array. Present so the pair distinguishes "an absent optional array stays absent" from "the field is never read at all".
items.name: Bank

items.note: An identity as 0.6.0 wrote one. addressSchema gained street2 and identityAddressSchema gained deliveryNotes in 0.7.0, so every identity stored before that release carries a five-field address.

address.deliveryNotes: Ring twice, leave with the concierge.

items.note: A card as 0.6.0 wrote one: its billingAddress predates street2. A card never has deliveryNotes in any release — the base address schema strips it — so this row also pins that the two address shapes did not converge.
items.name: Travel card

items.note: A note carrying only its content. noteDataSchema.format is .optional().default("markdown"), so this row is the one place the fixture exercises a DEFAULT being injected into an older document rather than a field simply staying absent.
items.name: Router details

items.note: A secret carrying an absolute ISO 8601 expiry with an explicit offset. expiresAt is read back through new Date(), so the stored string is an instant rather than a wall-clock reading, and it must survive a decrypt byte for byte.
items.name: Deploy token

folders.note: An ordinary folder. sourceRefId is stamped only on a fresh restore insert, so the overwhelming majority of real folders have never carried the key at all.
folders.name: Personal

folders.note: A nested folder, also without sourceRefId, so the parent edge is exercised on a row that lacks the optional field.
folders.name: Personal / Finance

folders.note: The counterpart: a folder that DID come from a restore and carries another account’s ObjectId in sourceRefId. Present so "an absent sourceRefId is accepted" is not confused with "sourceRefId is ignored", and so the never-serialize rule has something to hide.
folders.name: Restored

refreshTokens.note: Every refresh row written before 0.5.0, and every non-remembered session since: no absoluteExpiresAt at all. By design this must keep sliding by REFRESH_TOKEN_DAYS on each rotation, with no migration. Seeded PARTIALLY ELAPSED (2 days left, not a fresh 7) on purpose: a row seeded at the full horizon is indistinguishable from one a rotation just minted, so a rotation that carried the old expiry forward instead of sliding it would land inside any sane tolerance and the test would not see the defect it exists to catch.
The 0.5.0-era counterpart: a remembered family whose hard deadline rotation must carry forward unchanged rather than slide.
